description: Composite figure of four spin-resolved total density-of-states (DOS) plots computed by DFT for four κ-carbide compositions, delivered as two cropped images: panels (a) and (b) in the upper image, panels (c) and (d) in the lower image. All four panels share one format — a single green DOS trace split by a horizontal dotted line at the Fermi level into an upper (spin-up, plotted upwards) and a lower (spin-down, plotted downwards) half, plus a pair of dashed vertical arrows, one pointing up above the dotted line and one pointing down below it, placed at positive E − E_f. The x-axis is labelled "E − Ef (eV)" (title printed below panels c and d; the upper two panels show only the ticks), with tick labels −6, 0 and 4 eV. No y-axis is labelled or scaled in any panel, so DOS magnitudes cannot be quantified. Every panel shows the same peak sequence: peaks at the far left of the window, a cluster of sharp peaks near the middle, and finite DOS across the dotted Fermi-level line. The caption assigns the panels to Fe3AlC, Fe2MnAlC, FeMn2AlC and Mn3AlC (subscripts lost in the caption OCR). The figure demonstrates that the four κ-carbides have nearly identical DOS shapes that differ essentially only by a rigid band shift.
measured_quantities: total density of states (arbitrary units, y-axis unlabelled)

observations.observation: Each of the four panels plots a single green total-DOS trace divided by a horizontal dotted line into an upper (spin-up, drawn upward) and lower (spin-down, drawn downward) half, i.e. spin-resolved DOS with the Fermi level at the dotted line.
The x-axis of every panel is labelled E − Ef (eV) (the title is printed below panels (c) and (d) only) with visible tick labels −6, 0 and 4.
No y-axis label, tick values or scale bar appears in any of the four panels, so absolute DOS magnitudes cannot be read from the figure.
A pair of dashed vertical arrows — one pointing up in the spin-up half, one pointing down in the spin-down half — is drawn in every panel at positive E − E_f (slightly right of the 0 tick).

The peak sequence (sharp peaks at low E − E_f, a cluster of sharp peaks near the middle of the window, a smaller structure on the right) is closely repeated in all four panels, with only slight horizontal displacement of the features.
Finite DOS is present at the dotted Fermi-level line in all four panels, consistent with metallic character of the four κ-carbides.

The caption identifies the four panels as the total DOS of (a) Fe AlC, (b) Fe MnAlC, (c) FeMn2AlC and (d) Mn3AlC, i.e. the stoichiometric κ-carbides Fe3AlC, Fe2MnAlC, FeMn2AlC and Mn3AlC with subscripts lost in the caption text.
The citing text states that the overall shapes of the DOS of the four structures were very similar and that the only difference was a 'rigid band shift'.
The citing text states the rigid band shift corresponds either to the shift of peaks to higher energy or, equivalently, to the shift of the Fermi level to lower energy.
The citing text attributes the shift to two effects: Mn has one less electron than Fe, and the replacement of Fe by Mn barely produces a change in the electronic states around the Fermi level.
The citing text describes the four phases as crystalline κ-carbides.

subfigures.description: Spin-resolved total DOS of Fe3AlC (κ-carbide): green trace split by a dotted horizontal line at E_f into an upward spin-up and downward spin-down half, with a pair of dashed vertical arrows at positive E − E_f. X ticks −6, 0, 4 eV; x-axis title omitted in this crop; no y-axis scale.
Spin-resolved total DOS of Fe2MnAlC (Mn substituted for part of the Fe), same up/down dotted-line format and the same dashed up/down arrow pair; peak pattern nearly identical in shape to (a).
Spin-resolved total DOS of FeMn2AlC, same format; x-axis title 'E − Ef (eV)' printed below this panel. Peak positions resemble those of (a) and (b) with the features slightly displaced along E − E_f.

Spin-resolved total DOS of Mn3AlC, same format with x-axis title 'E − Ef (eV)'; the dashed arrow pair sits furthest to the right among the four panels and the peak fine structure again closely mirrors the other three compositions.
